title: Big-ticket purchase research (reliability + price)
description: Research a car, major appliance, mattress, or similar big-ticket item on reliability and price timing before deciding whether to buy now or wait.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: major-purchase-research
  title: Big-ticket purchase research (reliability + price)
  description: Research a car, major appliance, mattress, or similar big-ticket item on reliability and price timing before deciding whether to buy now or wait.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Help a shopper decide whether now is a good time to buy a specific big-ticket item, and which option is likely to hold up.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 3
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor: []
  nodes:
    - id: intake
      kind: input
      name: Purchase details and candidates
      summary: The item being considered, budget, and any candidate models or offers.
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required: [text]
        properties:
          text: { type: string, description: The item being considered, budget, timeline, and any specific models or offers to research. }
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: reliability-researcher
      kind: agent
      inlineRole: true
      name: Reliability and reviews researcher
      summary: Looks into long-term reliability, common failure points, and owner satisfaction.
      role: Researcher focused on how well an item holds up over years of ownership.
      prompt: Research the reliability track record, common failure points, and long-term owner satisfaction for the candidate item or models. Weigh recurring, well-evidenced patterns over single anecdotes, and flag any review source that looks incentivized or low-trust rather than treating it at face value. Do not state a specific failure rate or statistic unless it is actually available; otherwise describe the pattern qualitatively and note the uncertainty.
      capabilities: { skills: [research], tools: [read, search], permissions: [read-only] }
      outputSchema: { type: object }
    - id: price-timing-researcher
      kind: agent
      inlineRole: true
      name: Price history and timing researcher
      summary: Looks into typical price movement, sale cycles, and whether now looks like a good time to buy.
      role: Researcher focused on price trends and purchase timing for a category of big-ticket item.
      prompt: Research typical price behavior and sale cycles for this category of item, such as seasonal patterns, model-year turnover, or upcoming events that tend to move price. Describe the general pattern and how the current moment compares to it, without inventing a specific historical price point you cannot support. Note explicitly when the available information is too thin to say whether waiting would help.
      capabilities: { skills: [finance-analysis], tools: [read, search], permissions: [read-only] }
      outputSchema: { type: object }
    - id: research-group
      kind: group
      name: Parallel purchase research
      summary: Run the reliability researcher and the price timing researcher side by side.
      config: { members: [reliability-researcher, price-timing-researcher], execution: parallel, exit: aggregate }
    - id: merge-research
      kind: aggregator
      name: Merge research findings
      summary: Combine the reliability and timing findings into one picture of the candidate item.
      config: { aggregation: merge }
    - id: value-evaluate
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Buy timing evaluation
      summary: Weigh reliability confidence against price timing to recommend buying now or waiting.
      role: Neutral evaluator balancing reliability confidence against purchase timing.
      prompt: Using the merged research, weigh how confident the reliability findings are against how favorable the current price timing looks, and recommend either buying now or waiting for a better window. Be explicit about what would have to be true for the recommendation to flip, and lower confidence when either researcher flagged thin evidence. Do not invent a specific price or reliability statistic that was not already supplied.
      capabilities: { skills: [evaluation], tools: [read, calculate], permissions: [read-only] }
      outputSchema: { type: object, required: [score, passed, reasons, recommendedAction], properties: { score: { type: number }, passed: { type: boolean }, reasons: { type: array, items: { type: string } }, recommendedAction: { type: string, enum: [buy, wait] } } }
      config: { threshold: 0.7 }
    - id: timing-decision
      kind: condition
      name: Buy now or wait
      summary: Route to the matching recommendation based on the evaluation.
      config: { expression: "value-evaluate.recommendedAction", branches: [ { label: "Buy now", when: "buy" }, { label: "Wait for a better window", when: "wait" } ] }
    - id: result
      kind: output
      name: Purchase timing recommendation
      summary: Whether to buy now or wait, with the reliability and price reasoning behind it.
  edges:
    - { id: e1, from: intake, to: research-group, kind: data }
    - { id: e2, from: research-group, to: merge-research, kind: data }
    - { id: e3, from: merge-research, to: value-evaluate, kind: data }
    - { id: e4, from: value-evaluate, to: timing-decision, kind: data }
    - { id: e5, from: timing-decision, to: result, kind: control, condition: "buy" }
    - { id: e6, from: timing-decision, to: result, kind: control, condition: "wait" }
